name: Katrina
why: Price cut; Lagoon-sanctioned bulkhead work + standing rigging 2024; starboard engine replaced; renovated interior.
risks: Port engine ~6,800h, no lithium, weak solar/AC/generator setup; modernization burden is significant.
next_step: Keep as fallback value play; contact only if price drops further or stronger candidates fail diligence.
notes: Project penalty keeps it below stronger refit boats.

name: After Glow
why: Excellent Voyage 480 offshore platform; recent engine/saildrive work, 2023 genoa, 800-GPD watermaker, full A/C, paid storage through Nov. 2026, and seller now appears realistically reachable around $350k.
risks: Original standing rigging/main; 15,404h genset; no solar/radar/AIS/backup autopilot; only 2×255Ah Lifeline AGM house bank. 2026 West End invoice documents invasive port-hull core/skin repair for soft/delaminated areas and a PORT rudder recore with an ovaled rudder-stock exit hole—conflicting with earlier broker statement that STARBOARD rudder had moisture. This discrepancy plus composite repairs needs independent survey scrutiny.
all_in_display: ~$420–460k at ~$350k deal + survey/closing, potentially higher if rig/genset or repair findings expand
next_step: YOUR DECISION: only continue if the Voyage platform is attractive enough to justify a heavily survey-protected offer materially below $350k. Require surveyor to inspect port-hull core repair, rudder-side discrepancy, rig and genset. No call/offer initiated.
notes: West End Boatyard Apr. 2026 invoice subtotal $10,880: opened hull skins, removed damaged core, vacuum-bonded Divinycell + structural E-glass, repaired internal bilge laminate; recored port rudder and addressed ovaled stock exit. Broker says ~$350k likely acceptable.

name: Before Sunrise
why: Documented private-use refit: recall-replacement Volvo D1-30 engines (2023), 2023 rigging, 2025 furler and saildrive service, 1,885W solar, 600Ah Relion lithium/Victron, 7.5kW Onan, three A/C units and 140L/h watermaker. Current public ask has now fallen to $319k and seller previously indicated high-$200s/low-$300s offers are discussable.
risks: Original 2015 sails and likely original saildrives. Bottom/keels were stripped to gelcoat in 2023 to repair blistering with polyester filler before barrier coating; needs survey/moisture validation. Canadian registration/import status, battery health and owner confirmation of damage/structural history remain open.
next_step: Wait for the owner confirmations/invoices already promised. YOUR DECISION: accept or decline the offered live video tour after those arrive; no travel discussion needed yet.
notes: Fresh 9/3 public price reduction from $330k to $319k strengthens the value case. Maintenance log remains unusually detailed; survey should focus on 2023 blister/core work plus original sails/saildrives.

name: Santai
why: 2019 Lagoon 40 at genuine sub-$250k fleet-exit pricing; newer platform, documented Navigare maintenance, 45hp Yanmars and strong value even after a meaningful liveaboard refit.
risks: Ex-charter since new; ~3,836/3,842h engines; published spec is basic for off-grid use (560Ah service bank, no meaningful solar/lithium/watermaker package shown); need phase-out survey, structural/damage history, saildrive service and rig/sail condition.
next_step: Get maintenance file + phase-out work list; verify grounding/collision/storm/insurance history, saildrive seals/diaphragms, standing rigging and sail condition; test seller flexibility.
notes: NEW PRIORITY: confirms the 2018–20 Lagoon 40 market has multiple ~$250–290k opportunities. Available out of fleet 2026-11-30; tax not paid per YachtWorld.

name: Le Marin Lagoon 40
why: Very low entry price for a 2018 Lagoon 40; 45hp Yanmars, 3x115W solar, 2kW inverter, B&G electronics and 4-cabin/4-head layout leave substantial budget for liveaboard upgrades.
risks: ~3,960h engines; small solar/electrical baseline; need saildrive service history, rig age, structural/moisture history, damage/insurance history and clarity on generator/near-term capex.
next_step: No further diligence; preserve as a comp and keep NetBoat relationship warm for similar 2018+ Lagoon inventory.
notes: Carla Bianchini / NetBoat confirmed the 2018 Le Marin Lagoon 40 has sold. Archive from active ranking.

name: Grenada Lagoon 40
why: 2019 Lagoon 40 in Grenada at roughly mid-$200k equivalent; newer platform in ideal Caribbean geography with enough purchase-price headroom to build the off-grid spec ourselves.
risks: Public listing is sparse; need fleet/phase-out records, engine/saildrive hours and service, rig/sails, structural/damage history and actual onboard electrical/water systems.
next_step: Get phase-out/maintenance file, survey, damage history, saildrive/rig/sails and seller flexibility.
notes: Strong geography + age/price play; compare directly with Larimar and Santai.

name: Hodge Creek Lagoon 40
why: 2018 Lagoon 40 in the BVI around the high-$200k equivalent; ideal starting geography and likely fleet-exit economics with room for targeted liveaboard modernization.
risks: Ex-charter/fleet history needs full diligence; public listing lacks engine hours and detailed service history; need phase-out report, damage/insurance history, saildrives, rig and sails.
next_step: Get phase-out/handback file, maintenance/damage history, saildrive/rig/sails and realistic negotiation range.
notes: Caribbean fleet-exit comp; less compelling than the €230k 2019 Grenada boat unless condition is materially better.
